outcome: Counts on and back in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s from 0, and finds 10 or 100 more or less than any number.
prerequisites: Y2.NPV.1 counting in steps of 2, 3, 5 and 10s; Y2.NPV.2 two-digit place value
vocabulary: multiple, step, more than, less than, 10 more, 100 more
examples: Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24 …; 10 less than 347 is 337; 100 more than 590 is 690
gap: Counting in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s as a sequence skill is not taught; 'more or less' is.

outcome: Says the value of each digit in a 3-digit number.
prerequisites: Y2.NPV.2 place value of two-digit numbers
vocabulary: digit, hundreds, tens, ones, place value
examples: In 546 the 4 is worth 40; 603 has no tens

outcome: Compares and orders numbers up to 1,000.
prerequisites: Y2.NPV.4 compare and order to 100 with <, > and =; Y3.NPV.2
vocabulary: greater than, less than, order, ascending, descending

outcome: Identifies, represents and estimates numbers using different representations.
prerequisites: Y2.NPV.3 representations including the number line; Y3.NPV.2
vocabulary: represent, estimate, number line, base ten, place-value chart
examples: Show 346 with blocks; estimate where 700 sits on a 0–1,000 line
gap: Estimating position on a number line is not taught; place-value charts and partitioning are.

outcome: Reads and writes numbers up to 1,000 in numerals and words.
prerequisites: Y2.NPV.5 read and write to 100 in numerals and words

outcome: Solves number and practical problems using place value up to 1,000.
examples: A shop has 245 cards; 100 more arrive. How many now?
gap: Problem solving is mostly within-skill; no explicit practical-problem content.

outcome: Adds and subtracts mentally: a 3-digit number and 1s, 10s or 100s.
prerequisites: Y2.AS.3 mental addition and subtraction; Y3.NPV.1
vocabulary: mentally, add, subtract, total, difference, more than, less than

outcome: Adds and subtracts numbers up to 3 digits using columns.
gap: The island goes to 4 digits, beyond Year 3.

outcome: Estimates an answer and uses the inverse operation to check it.
examples: Estimate 398 + 204 as about 600; check 734 − 258 by adding

outcome: Solves problems, including missing-number problems, with addition and subtraction.
vocabulary: missing number, problem, total, difference, bar model

outcome: Recalls and uses multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4 and 8 times tables.
vocabulary: multiply, divide, times table, product, multiple, factor

outcome: Writes and calculates multiplication and division statements, including 2-digit × 1-digit, mentally then by a written method.
prerequisites: Y3.MD.1; Y2.MD.2 writing statements with ×, ÷ and =
gap: Short multiplication is in the island from Year 4 numbers up; mental partitioning for 2-digit × 1-digit is partly covered.

outcome: Solves multiplication and division problems, including missing-number, scaling and correspondence problems.
vocabulary: scaling, times as many, correspondence, missing number
examples: '3 hats and 4 scarves: how many outfits?'; 'times as many as'
gap: Correspondence (n objects to m objects) is covered by 'counting choices' only.

outcome: Counts up and down in tenths; knows tenths come from splitting a whole into 10 equal parts and from dividing a one-digit number or quantity by 10.
prerequisites: Y2.FRAC.1 fractions of a shape and quantity; Y2.MD.1 the 10 times table
vocabulary: tenth, tenths, equal parts, divide by 10
gap: Tenths are taught as decimals on the Decimals preview, not as counting in tenths or dividing by 10; not in the R1 Fractions island.

outcome: Recognises, finds and writes fractions of a set of objects: unit and non-unit fractions with small denominators.
prerequisites: Y2.FRAC.1; Y2.FRAC.2; Y3.MD.1 division facts for sharing
vocabulary: unit fraction, non-unit fraction, numerator, denominator, of a set
gap: Fractions of amounts are taught (lesson 'amounts'); the sharing step needs division facts. `fractions.equal-parts` supports this objective: the statutory text does not name equal parts as a separate objective, but unit fractions presuppose them (Year 2: Y2.FRAC.1).

outcome: Recognises and uses fractions as numbers: unit and non-unit fractions with small denominators.
vocabulary: fraction, number line, numerator, denominator, between
examples: Place 3/4 on a 0–1 line; 1/4 is a number between 0 and 1
gap: Number line runs 0 to 1 only; fractions above 1 are deferred.

outcome: Recognises and shows, using diagrams, equivalent fractions with small denominators.
vocabulary: equivalent, equal, same amount, fraction wall

outcome: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same denominator within one whole.
vocabulary: denominator, same denominator, add, subtract, whole
gap: Not taught in the R1 Fractions island; the Fractions 2 preview covers it (and the Year 4 and 5 versions).

outcome: Compares and orders unit fractions, and fractions with the same denominator.
vocabulary: compare, order, greater than, less than, same whole, bigger denominator

outcome: Solves problems that involve all of the above.
vocabulary: problem, fraction of a set, compare, explain
examples: 'Tom ate 2/8 and Mia 3/8 of a pizza: who ate more?'
gap: Problems with tenths and with adding the same denominator sit outside the R1 island.

outcome: Measures, compares, adds and subtracts lengths (m/cm/mm), mass (kg/g) and capacity (l/ml).
prerequisites: Y2.MEAS.1 standard units; Y2.MEAS.2 compare measures
vocabulary: length, mass, capacity, metre, centimetre, millimetre, kilogram, gram, litre, millilitre
examples: Add 2 m 30 cm and 85 cm; which jug holds more?
gap: No island teaches measuring or adding lengths, mass and capacity.

outcome: Measures the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
examples: Perimeter of a 3 cm by 5 cm rectangle

outcome: Adds and subtracts amounts of money to give change, using £ and p in practical contexts.
prerequisites: Y2.MEAS.3 £ and p; Y2.MEAS.5 simple money problems, including change

outcome: Tells and writes the time from an analogue clock, including Roman numerals I to XII, and 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
vocabulary: analogue, digital, Roman numerals, 12-hour, 24-hour, o'clock, past, to
examples: Read 7:42 on a clock face with Roman numerals
gap: Roman numerals on clocks are not taught.

outcome: Estimates and reads time to the nearest minute; records and compares time in seconds, minutes and hours; uses a.m./p.m. vocabulary.
prerequisites: Y3.MEAS.4; Y2.MEAS.8 minutes in an hour
vocabulary: second, minute, hour, a.m., p.m., morning, afternoon, noon, midnight
examples: 'Half past three in the afternoon' is 3:30 p.m.
gap: The vocabulary noon and midnight is not specifically taught.

outcome: Knows the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year.
vocabulary: second, minute, month, year, leap year
examples: 60 seconds in a minute; 366 days in a leap year
gap: Days in each month and leap years are not confirmed in the lesson description.

outcome: Compares durations of events, for example calculates the time taken by tasks.
examples: A film starts at 2:15 and ends at 3:50: how long?

outcome: Draws 2-D shapes and makes 3-D shapes; recognises 3-D shapes in different orientations and describes them.
examples: Name a cuboid turned on its side
gap: Drawing and making shapes with modelling materials is a practical activity the screens can't deliver.

outcome: Recognises angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn.
examples: The corner of a square; a quarter turn

outcome: Identifies right angles; knows 2 right angles make a half-turn, 3 three-quarters and 4 a full turn; says whether an angle is greater or less than a right angle.
vocabulary: right angle, half turn, quarter turn, three-quarter turn, full turn
examples: Is this angle bigger or smaller than a right angle?

outcome: Identifies horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines.
examples: Which two edges of a window are parallel?
gap: Line relationships are not taught by any island.

outcome: Interprets and presents data using bar charts, pictograms and tables.
prerequisites: Y2.STAT.1 pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and tables
vocabulary: bar chart, pictogram, table, key, scale, axis
examples: Read a pictogram where one symbol is 2 children
gap: Reading is taught; presenting (drawing) data is not.

outcome: Solves one-step and two-step 'how many more/fewer' questions using scaled bar charts, pictograms and tables.
vocabulary: how many more, how many fewer, total, scale
examples: 'How many more children chose football than rugby?'

outcome: Counts in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25 and 1,000.
vocabulary: multiple, step, count on, count back
gap: Multiples as times-table facts are taught; counting 25s and 1,000s is not.

outcome: Finds 1,000 more or less than a given number.
Counts backwards through 0 to include negative numbers.
vocabulary: negative, below zero, minus, number line

outcome: Says the value of each digit in a 4-digit number.
Orders and compares numbers beyond 1,000.
Identifies, represents and estimates numbers using different representations.
vocabulary: represent, estimate, number line, place-value chart
gap: Estimating on a number line is not taught.

outcome: Rounds any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000.
Solves number and practical problems with all of the above and increasingly large positive numbers.
examples: A school has 1,250 books; 1,000 more arrive

outcome: Reads Roman numerals to 100 (I to C) and knows the numeral system changed over time to include 0 and place value.
prerequisites: Y3.MEAS.4 Roman numerals I to XII
vocabulary: Roman numeral, numeral system, place value, zero
gap: Roman numerals are not taught beyond clock faces; no island covers them.

outcome: Adds and subtracts numbers with up to 4 digits using columns where appropriate.
Estimates and uses inverse operations to check answers.
Solves addition and subtraction two-step problems, deciding which operations and methods to use and why.
examples: 'A bus has 48 seats; 27 are taken, then 9 get off'
gap: Explaining 'why' a method was chosen is not a graded step in the lessons.

outcome: Recalls multiplication and division facts up to 12 × 12.
gap: The Year 4 Multiplication Tables Check (MTC) format is R2 (TT epic), not here.

outcome: Uses place value, known and derived facts to multiply and divide mentally, including × by 0 and 1, ÷ by 1 and multiplying 3 numbers.
vocabulary: derived fact, mentally, multiply by 0, multiply together
gap: Multiplying by 0 and 1, and three numbers, are not confirmed in the lesson descriptions.

outcome: Recognises and uses factor pairs and commutativity in mental calculations.
gap: Commutativity in mental calculation is not specifically taught.

outcome: Multiplies 2-digit and 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number using a formal written layout.
Solves problems with multiplying and adding, using the distributive law, integer scaling and harder correspondence problems.
gap: The distributive law is used implicitly (partitioning) but not named.

outcome: Recognises and shows, using diagrams, families of common equivalent fractions.
vocabulary: equivalent, family of fractions, fraction wall, multiply top and bottom

outcome: Counts up and down in hundredths; knows hundredths arise when dividing an object by 100 and tenths by 10.
gap: Hundredths are taught as decimal places on the preview island; counting in hundredths as fractions is not.

outcome: Solves problems that find fractions of quantities and divide quantities, including non-unit fractions with a whole-number answer.
vocabulary: fraction of a quantity, unit fraction, non-unit fraction, share equally

outcome: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same denominator.
gap: Not in the R1 Fractions island; preview only.

outcome: Recognises and writes decimal equivalents of any number of tenths or hundredths.
vocabulary: decimal, decimal point, tenths, hundredths, equivalent

outcome: Recognises and writes decimal equivalents to 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.
Finds the effect of dividing a 1- or 2-digit number by 10 and 100, giving digit values as ones, tenths and hundredths.
vocabulary: divide by 10, divide by 100, tenths, hundredths

outcome: Rounds decimals with 1 decimal place to the nearest whole number.
vocabulary: round, decimal place, nearest whole number

outcome: Compares numbers with the same number of decimal places up to 2 decimal places.
gap: Comparing numbers with different numbers of decimal places is a known misconception area; 'same number of places' is the statutory scope.

outcome: Solves simple measure and money problems involving fractions and decimals to 2 decimal places.
gap: Measure contexts are not taught beyond money.

outcome: Converts between units of measure, for example km to m and hours to minutes.
gap: Only time units are converted; length, mass and capacity conversions are not taught.

outcome: Measures and calculates the perimeter of rectilinear figures, including squares, in cm and m.
examples: Perimeter of an L-shape with labelled sides

outcome: Finds the area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares.
Estimates, compares and calculates different measures, including money in pounds and pence.
examples: About how heavy is this book?
gap: Only money measures are covered.

outcome: Reads, writes and converts time between analogue and digital 12- and 24-hour clocks.
Solves problems converting hours to minutes, minutes to seconds, years to months and weeks to days.
Compares and classifies geometric shapes, including quadrilaterals and triangles, by properties and sizes.
vocabulary: quadrilateral, triangle, equilateral, isosceles, scalene, parallelogram, rhombus, trapezium
examples: Name a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides

outcome: Identifies acute and obtuse angles and compares and orders angles up to 2 right angles by size.
examples: Order three angles from smallest to largest

outcome: Identifies lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes in different orientations.
vocabulary: line of symmetry, reflect, mirror, orientation
examples: How many lines of symmetry has a square?
gap: Symmetry is not taught by any island.

outcome: Completes a simple symmetric figure with respect to a specific line of symmetry.
examples: Finish the picture so it is symmetric about the dotted line
gap: Not taught; needs a drawing interaction.

outcome: Describes positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant.
vocabulary: coordinates, x, y, axis, grid, first quadrant

outcome: Describes movements between positions as translations of a given unit left/right and up/down.
examples: Move (2, 1) three right and one up to (5, 2)

outcome: Plots specified points and draws sides to complete a given polygon.
gap: Completing polygons is partly covered (missing corner); drawing sides is not.

outcome: Interprets and presents discrete and continuous data using bar charts and time graphs.
vocabulary: bar chart, time graph, discrete, continuous, scale
gap: Reading is taught; presenting data is not.

outcome: Solves comparison, sum and difference problems using bar charts, pictograms, tables and other graphs.
examples: 'How much warmer at noon than at 8 a.m.?'

outcome: Reads, writes, orders and compares numbers to at least 1,000,000 and gives the value of each digit.
vocabulary: million, hundred thousand, ten thousand, digit, value

outcome: Counts forwards or backwards in steps of powers of 10 from any number up to 1,000,000.
Interprets negative numbers in context and counts with positive and negative whole numbers, including through 0.
vocabulary: negative, temperature, below zero, through zero
examples: From −3 °C a rise of 5 degrees gives 2 °C

outcome: Rounds any number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000.
vocabulary: round, nearest, ten thousand, hundred thousand

outcome: Solves number and practical problems involving all of the above.
examples: A stadium holds 56,300: round to the nearest 1,000

outcome: Reads Roman numerals to 1,000 (M) and recognises years written in Roman numerals.
vocabulary: Roman numeral, M, D, C, year
gap: Not taught.

outcome: Adds and subtracts whole numbers with more than 4 digits, including by columns.
gap: The island description names numbers up to 4 digits; numbers with more than 4 digits are not confirmed.

outcome: Adds and subtracts numbers mentally with increasingly large numbers.
gap: Mental strategies are taught for smaller numbers; 'increasingly large' is not confirmed. Mental Maths strategy work is R3 (MM epic).

outcome: Uses rounding to check answers and decides the level of accuracy needed in a problem.
examples: Round to check 4,872 + 2,119; is an estimate enough here?
gap: Deciding the level of accuracy needed in context is not specifically taught.

outcome: Solves multi-step addition and subtraction problems, deciding which operations and methods to use and why.
gap: Island problems are two-step; 'multi-step' beyond two steps is not confirmed.

outcome: Identifies multiples and factors, including all factor pairs of a number and common factors of 2 numbers.
vocabulary: multiple, factor, factor pair, common factor
gap: Common factors of two numbers are not confirmed.

outcome: Knows and uses the vocabulary of prime numbers, prime factors and composite numbers.
gap: Primes are not taught.

outcome: Establishes whether a number up to 100 is prime and recalls primes up to 19.
gap: Not taught.

outcome: Multiplies numbers up to 4 digits by a 1- or 2-digit number using a formal method, including long multiplication for 2-digit numbers.
vocabulary: long multiplication, short multiplication, partial product

outcome: Multiplies and divides mentally, drawing on known facts.
gap: Mental Maths strategies are R3 (MM epic).

outcome: Divides numbers up to 4 digits by a 1-digit number using short division and interprets remainders appropriately.
Multiplies and divides whole numbers and those with decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000.
gap: The decimals island covers × and ÷ by 10 and 100, not 1,000.

outcome: Recognises and uses square and cube numbers and the notation ² and ³.
vocabulary: square number, cube number, squared, cubed
gap: Not taught.

outcome: Solves multiplication and division problems using factors, multiples, squares and cubes.
examples: 'Which number less than 50 is a square and a multiple of 3?'

outcome: Solves problems with all four operations and combinations, including the meaning of the equals sign.
gap: The equals sign as 'is the same as' is not specifically taught.

outcome: Solves multiplication and division problems including scaling by simple fractions and simple rates.
examples: 'A recipe for 4 uses 300 g; for 6?'; 'Cost per metre'

outcome: Compares and orders fractions whose denominators are all multiples of the same number.
gap: The R1 comparing lesson covers same denominator or same numerator and unit fractions; different denominators that are multiples are not confirmed.

outcome: Identifies, names and writes equivalent fractions of a given fraction, shown visually, including tenths and hundredths.
Recognises mixed numbers and improper fractions, converts between them, and writes statements greater than 1 as a mixed number.
vocabulary: mixed number, improper fraction, whole, convert
gap: Not in the R1 Fractions island; fractions greater than 1 are deferred there.

outcome: Adds and subtracts fractions with the same denominator and with denominators that are multiples of the same number.
Multiplies proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by materials and diagrams.
vocabulary: multiply, whole number, mixed number, diagram
gap: The preview multiplies a fraction by a whole number; mixed numbers are not confirmed.

outcome: Reads and writes decimal numbers as fractions.
Recognises and uses thousandths and relates them to tenths, hundredths and decimal equivalents.
gap: Thousandths are not taught.

outcome: Rounds decimals with 2 decimal places to the nearest whole number and to 1 decimal place.
Reads, writes, orders and compares numbers with up to 3 decimal places.
gap: The decimals island covers tenths and hundredths, not 3 decimal places.

outcome: Solves problems involving numbers up to 3 decimal places.
Recognises the per cent symbol and that per cent means parts per 100; writes percentages as fractions with denominator 100 and as decimals.
vocabulary: per cent, percentage, out of 100, symbol %

outcome: Solves problems needing percentage and decimal equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and fractions with denominators that are multiples of 10 or 25.
Converts between metric units of measure.
vocabulary: kilometre, metre, centimetre, millimetre, gram, kilogram, litre, millilitre
gap: Unit conversion for length, mass and capacity is not taught.

outcome: Understands and uses approximate equivalences between metric and common imperial units.
gap: Not taught.

outcome: Measures and calculates the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in cm and m.
Calculates and compares the area of rectangles using cm² and m², and estimates the area of irregular shapes.
vocabulary: area, square centimetre, square metre, irregular
gap: Estimating the area of irregular shapes is not taught.

outcome: Estimates volume and capacity.
examples: Build a cuboid with 1 cm³ blocks
gap: Volume is not taught.

outcome: Solves problems converting between units of time.
Uses all four operations to solve measure problems with decimal notation, including scaling.
gap: Only money contexts are confirmed.

outcome: Identifies 3-D shapes, including cubes and other cuboids, from 2-D representations.
examples: Which 3-D shape does this drawing show?
gap: Recognising solids from drawings is not confirmed.

outcome: Knows angles are measured in degrees; estimates and compares acute, obtuse and reflex angles.
Draws given angles and measures them in degrees.
gap: Measuring and drawing with a protractor is not taught.

outcome: Identifies angles at a point (360°), on a straight line (180°) and multiples of 90°; uses rectangle properties to find missing lengths and angles; distinguishes regular and irregular polygons.
vocabulary: angles at a point, straight line, regular, irregular, polygon
examples: Find x where angles on a line are 110° and x
gap: Angles at a point and on a line are taught; rectangle properties and regular/irregular polygons are not confirmed.

outcome: Identifies, describes and represents the position of a shape after a reflection or translation, using appropriate language, and knows the shape has not changed.
examples: Reflect a triangle in a vertical line
gap: Translation is taught; reflection is not.

outcome: Solves comparison, sum and difference problems using information in a line graph.
examples: 'How much did it rise between 2 and 5?'

outcome: Completes, reads and interprets information in tables, including timetables.
examples: A bus timetable: when does the 09:40 arrive?

outcome: Reads, writes, orders and compares numbers up to 10,000,000 and gives the value of each digit.
gap: The island goes up to a million; 10,000,000 is not confirmed.

outcome: Rounds any whole number to a required degree of accuracy.
gap: Up to a million only.

outcome: Uses negative numbers in context and calculates intervals across 0.
examples: From −4 °C to 7 °C is a rise of 11 °C

outcome: Solves number and practical problems involving all of the above.
examples: A population rounded to the nearest 10,000

outcome: Solves problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
